synopsis: Tag-based systems are common in mining collision avoidance and can narrow what perception must prove, but their protection depends on people and machines being equipped; Epiroc Titan CAS and CAS Interface explicitly require everyone and every machine to be tagged [f4593, f12692, f1670]. Untagged people and objects fall outside cooperative sensing, so mixed fleets containing non-equipped objects need validation arguments for both tag-based and perception-based detection [f503, f2005]. Tag removal is a documented operational weakness: MSHA’s January 2017 notice recorded mechanics removing wearable tags to diagnose leaks in the red zone, while broader reports describe bypass requests and a false sense of security [f3297, f3034]. Position and message paths are comparatively easy to emulate and fault-inject, but validation still requires physical evidence for coverage, radio propagation, synchronisation and tag failure; the corpus found neither simulation-fidelity studies for these proximity technologies nor validated simulation of propagation around large metal machines [f500, f502, f4598, f4599]. Testing must distinguish physical radio/interface stimulation from downstream measurement injection, and deployment planning must address interoperability: mines may mix systems, while the glossary reports that devices from different suppliers did not interoperate [f5323, f7484, f12690].
